answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks via a pulse-linked bonding thread: every new identity must lock a capital bond that grows with network size and can only be unlocked after a fixed number of consecutive epochs of attested activity on the same thread; identities that wander in as fresh clones forfeit the bond on early exit or failed challenges, so an attacker creating thousands of fakes must immobilize proportional capital for weeks while risking total loss, rendering mass fabrication uneconomical compared to honest long-term participation.
